cohort: The study included all women undergoing cesarean section at or after 28 weeks gestation in a tertiary care center in Jammu, India, between November 2022 and January 2024.
finding: The study revealed a high cesarean section rate (35%) in the tertiary care center, primarily driven by repeat cesarean sections (37%) and fetal distress (23%), with favorable maternal and neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The study identified a high cesarean section rate, primarily driven by repeat cesarean sections and fetal distress, necessitating strategies to optimize rates.
gest_age: greater than or equal to 28 weeks gestation
